title: A mini test runner
description:
`cargo test` runs each test function and reports which ones panicked. Write the core of such a runner:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
enum Outcome { Passed, Failed(String), Ignored }

struct TestCase { name: &'static str, ignored: bool, body: fn() }

fn run_tests(tests: &[TestCase], filter: &str) -> Vec<(String, Outcome)>
fn summary(results: &[(String, Outcome)]) -> String
```

- `run_tests` runs every test whose name **contains** `filter` (all of them for `""`), in order. A test passes if its body returns normally, fails with the panic message if it panics, and is `Ignored` without running if `ignored` is set.
- Catch panics with `std::panic::catch_unwind`. The panic message is the payload as a `&str` or `String` (for `panic!("x {}", 1)` it is a `String`); anything else is reported as `"panic"`.
- Silence the default panic output while the tests run (`std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(|_| {}))`), and restore the previous hook afterwards with `take_hook`/`set_hook`.
- `summary` gives `"test result: FAILED. 2 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored"`, or `ok` instead of `FAILED` when nothing failed.
hints: `catch_unwind` takes a closure (or a plain `fn()`) and returns `Err(payload)` if it panicked (the payload's type is `Box<dyn std::any::Any + Send>`: a value of unknown type); `payload.downcast_ref::<&str>()` and `downcast_ref::<String>()` recover the message.
`let previous = panic::take_hook();` saves the current hook; install a silent one while running, then `panic::set_hook(previous)` to put it back.
